title: FigureLab: a browser-based tool for assembling publication-quality scientific figures
description:
FigureLab is a single-file, browser-based application for assembling publication-quality scientific figures from image data (microscopy, western blots, histology, gels, and clinical or specimen photographs). It runs entirely client-side with no installation, server, or internet connection required, so no image data ever leaves the user's computer.

Features include grid layout with drag-to-space gutters, per-panel image adjustments (brightness, contrast, gamma, levels, fluorescence LUTs, and multi-channel composites), two-point scale-bar calibration, an annotation system with undo/redo, and export to PNG, JPEG, WebP, TIFF, PDF, and SVG at publication DPI (up to 1200 dpi for line art). A freeform editor adds vector data charts (bar, line, scatter, box, heatmap, and Kaplan-Meier survival curves) generated from pasted or CSV/TSV data, flowcharts with connectors that stay anchored to their boxes (including PRISMA, CONSORT, and fishbone templates), object grouping, and a recolourable scientific-icon library. Scientific-integrity safeguards are built in by design: no p-value or statistical inference is ever computed (users enter significance symbols from their own tests), pixel edits are non-destructive reversible overlays, and any AI-generated content is disclosed in the figure's metadata and never applied to imported experimental images. It also exports reproducibility scripts (R/Python, including chart-generation code), CSV panel metadata, and journal-style captions.
